Here's the plan. Nothing has run yet. All I've done is build a trial copy of the reader's material in `scratchpad/` to see what a reader would get.

## What each reader gets

`quirework publish packet --prose-dir` produces 11 plain-text files and one image, and nothing else:

- the title page
- the preface
- the nine chapters, each opening with its Part's title or running head
- Hedda's screen, as a PNG

There is no spec, no sidecars, no alt text and no `AGENTS.md`. The copy will be mounted read-only at a path that doesn't name the book, the project or Quirework. I'd also add `mount_markers = ["side-quest", "quirework", "dequest"]` to `quirework.toml` so the tool refuses a mount path that gives the book away.

## The readers

| | Reader A | Reader B |
|---|---|---|
| Harness | Claude Code | Codex |
| Model | Sonnet (latest; the receipt records which version) | gpt-6.1-sol |
| Effort | medium | medium |

Neither one is Opus, the model you're talking to. They run separately, each in its own isolated environment, and neither sees the other's answers.

**Persona** (one, shared): "You picked up this book because the title and cover caught your eye. You don't know the author. Read it the way you'd read any book you chose yourself, and be honest when it loses you." I'm not telling them it's short, what it's about, or that anyone is worried about length.

## The questions

The readers open the files themselves, one at a time, in order. After each file, and before opening the next, they write a reaction file (`reactions/NN-name.md`) with four headings:

1. **Keep reading?** A number from 1 to 10, then one line on why.
2. **What I expect next.**
3. **What lost me, or what I didn't believe.** Quote the line if there is one.
4. **More or less?** Whether they wanted more of this chapter, less, or what it gave, and of what.

The title page counts as the first file, so we also get what they expect from the title alone.

**Closing question**, asked in a separate second turn after the read, so they never see it while reading: "What was this book about? Three sentences."

## What the tool checks for us

The run receipts show, per reader:

- every chapter was read in full, in order;
- each reaction was written before the next chapter was opened;
- the figure was actually opened, not judged from its caption;
- the model that answered.

If any of these is missing or fails, I'll tell you rather than present that reader's answers as clean.

## What I bring back

- A chapter-by-chapter table with both readers side by side: the score, what they expected, what lost them, and more or less.
- Where interest dips, and the reasons they gave.
- Every place either reader asked for more, kept separate from the overall word count.
- Their two three-sentence summaries.
- The one revision I'd make because of what they said.

On length: two model readers are evidence, not a verdict. I'll report what they said. Whether the twelve-thousand-word figure in `AGENTS.md` changes is your call, and I'll only write it down there once you've made it.

## Files, cost and records

**New files:**
- `procedures/personas/first-time-reader.json`
- `procedures/instruments/blind-read.json`
- a `self-driven` reader preset with `sops.personas` and `sops.instruments` pointing at those directories, in `quirework.toml`

**Cost:** two launches plus two short closing turns. Claude reports a price; Codex doesn't, so the Codex reader's spend will show as usage only.

**Records:** the runs go under `provenance/readings/`, added to `evidence_roots`. I'll commit the config and the records only when you say so, after `quirework dev check` passes.

Say go, or tell me what to change: models, persona wording, or questions.

# Reading: blind, whole book

The whole book was read blind on 2026-10-09 by two readers, on two
harnesses, each alone. Neither had the spec, the sidecars, this file or
anything else about the book: only the title page, the preface and the
nine chapters as plain text, and Hedda's screen as an image. Each opened
the chapters itself, one at a time, in order, and wrote a reaction to
each before opening the next. A closing question came only after the
last reaction, in a second turn, so neither saw it while reading.

The book they read was commit `a94ae30`, with no uncommitted edits.

`plan/` holds what the readers were asked: `reading.md` is the reading
turn as it was frozen, and `closing.md` the closing question. The engine
added only the paths to save each file under. The persona is
`procedures/personas/first-time-reader.json` and the questions are
`procedures/instruments/blind-read.json`. `reader-a/` and `reader-b/`
hold what each reader wrote, exactly as they saved it: one reaction per
file, named for the file it reacts to, and `wrap.md`, the answer to the
closing question. All of it is evidence, not the book: nothing reflows
it or holds it to the house rules. The raw run records, sessions and
receipts stay outside the book.

## The readers

| Reader | Harness | Model | Effort | Output tokens | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Claude Code | sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5) | medium | 6,849, of which 805 thinking | $0.20 for the reading turn, list-price equivalent under a subscription |
| B | Codex | gpt-6.1-sol | medium | 4,682 for both turns, of which 40 reasoning | not reported by the harness |

Input, as each harness reports it: A 28 plus 226,201 cache reads and
26,199 cache writes, for the reading turn; B 311,029 across both turns,
of which 286,720 cached, since Codex counts cached tokens inside its
input.

Both ran with the filesystem enforced and compaction refused, and none
was observed. Each passed the blindness canary before it launched, on
haiku and on gpt-6-luna. The book was mounted read-only at
`/home/ademar/library/book`, a path that names neither the book nor the
tool, and its digest held from planning to the end of each read.

## What the receipts proved

For both readers, the reading turn's receipt shows:

- all eleven files read in full, and in order;
- each reaction written before the next file was opened;
- the one figure opened (1 of 1), not judged from its caption;
- no red flags.

Reader B's closing turn completed with no red flags and wrote
`wrap.md`.

Reader A's closing turn did not complete in the record. The reader wrote
`wrap.md` in that turn, and its chat reply after it was shorter than the
200 bytes the plan asks of an answer, so the engine refused to bank the
turn and kept it pending. `reader-a/wrap.md` is the file the reader
wrote, copied byte for byte from its workspace; no receipt covers it.
It was not written during the reading turn, whose receipt lists the
eleven reactions and nothing else.

## Two things done by hand

The plan compiler puts the persona into the block of headings each
reaction must carry, and the engine also puts it at the top of the
first turn, so a reader would have seen it twice, once as if it were a
heading to copy. The instrument therefore names no persona, and the
persona was set on each seat in the compiled plan, which puts it once,
at the top. `plan/reading.md` shows the result.

The closing question was asked as approved. Its 200-byte floor is the
compiler's, measured against the chat reply rather than the file, which
is why Reader A's turn stopped.

## What they said

| | A: keep reading | B: keep reading |
|---|---|---|
| Title page | 6 | 7 |
| Preface | 7 | 8 |
| How's the Book? | 8 | 9 |
| Two Shops | 9 | 8 |
| Index Cards | 8 | 8 |
| Otto | 8 | 9 |
| The Name | 7 | 7 |
| Nine Hundred Lines | 8 | 8 |
| Em | 8 | 7 |
| The Demo | 9 | 9 |
| Full Stop | 8 | 8 |

Both readers, independently, found that Hedda's screen in The Demo does
not agree with the text around it. Reader A: chapter eight, which the
text names as where the corrected date came from, is not on the screen.
Reader B: chapter one's sentence, "No printer's manual gave the dash a
rule before 1684", does not contradict a first rule in 1694, so the
screen marks a disagreement that is not one. Both are right.

## What became of it

Not yet decided. Whether the book's length figure in `AGENTS.md`
changes is Cy's decision, and so is the revision.

## Blind read: what the two readers said

Both readers read the whole book in order, writing each reaction before opening the next chapter, and both opened the figure. The receipts show that for both reads, with no red flags.

- **Reader A:** Claude Code on Sonnet 5.5. The reading turn cost $0.20 at list price, under your subscription.
- **Reader B:** Codex on gpt-6.1-sol. The harness doesn't report a cost.

One gap: Reader A's closing answer isn't covered by a receipt. The reader wrote it, but its chat reply afterwards was under the 200-byte minimum, so the tool left that turn pending. The README in the record says so.

### Chapter by chapter (A / B)

| | Keep reading (A / B) | What lost them | More or less |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Title** | 6 / 7 | – | Both: start the book |
| **Preface** | 7 / 8 | A: "names changed… exaggerated" made them unsure what's true, and wary of a product pitch. B: "you have found something the software missed" is too neat after "I fixed most of them." | A: the shortness suits it. B: what it gave |
| **How's the Book?** | 8 / 9 | B: "I will come to that" made them impatient for the actual disagreement. | A: more Hedda. B: less of the ritual repeated, more of the manuscript |
| **Two Shops** | 9 / 8 | B didn't buy "Fashion doesn't happen twice," or that the contradiction can't be fixed. | A: more. B: more of what the sources said |
| **Index Cards** | 8 / 8 | **Both:** the script "found fourteen contradictions" with no example shown. A: "I write about software for a living" arrives late and feels convenient. | **Both: more of the script actually working** |
| **Otto** | 8 / 9 | Nothing serious. | **Both: right-sized** |
| **The Name** | **7 / 7** | A: "I write about software for a living" is repeated almost word for word. B: the reason it needed a name felt made up. | **Both: less naming, more of what the tool does** |
| **Nine Hundred Lines** | 8 / 8 | B: was asked to take the README's clarity on trust. | Both: right. B wanted a short quote from the README |
| **Em** | 8 / **7** | A: "in that order," and "I didn't write that check," didn't make sense to them. B: the three-dash riddle pulls away from the main story. | Both: less withholding, more of Em using the tool |
| **The Demo** | **9 / 9** | **Both: the figure doesn't match the text** (details below). | A: more of the demo. B: show examples like this earlier |
| **Full Stop** | 8 / 8 | B: "I've stopped minding" comes too quickly. | A: less explaining ("A tool built to avoid a book…"). B: a little more of writing *this* book |

**Where interest dips:** The Name is the low point for both readers, at 7 each, and both called it a pause in a story they wanted to move. Em dips for B, because the riddle pulls away from the main thread. Interest peaks at Two Shops for A, at How's the Book? and Otto for B, and at The Demo for both. Neither reader's score dropped below 7 after the title page.

**Is it too short anywhere?** Neither reader said the book was too short. Neither asked for a longer chapter except where something was missing:

- Index Cards, The Name and Em: show the tool doing something concrete.
- Full Stop (B only): a little more of how the change happened.

Both readers said The Name could be shorter, and both called Otto and Nine Hundred Lines the right length. On this evidence the book wants about the length it has, with three gaps filled. It doesn't need to grow toward twelve thousand words. Changing that figure in `AGENTS.md` is your call, so I haven't touched it.

**The closing question:** both summaries are accurate. Reader A wrote that the tool "ended up being how this other, shorter book got written and finished, while Full Stop stayed at eleven chapters." Reader B called it "a funny, self-questioning account of unreliable assistance, attachment to good sentences, and finishing something other than what he set out to write."

Reader B called you "he" all the way through. The book never states the narrator's pronouns, so a reader fills in a default. I'm noting it; I'm not proposing a fix.

## The one revision I'd make: fix Hedda's screen in The Demo

Both readers found this on their own, and in the book's highest-scoring chapter. I checked both points against the source, and both are real defects:

1. **Chapter eight is missing from the screen.** The text says you made chapter three agree with chapter eight, so chapter eight also makes the claim and should be listed. The screen shows only chapters 1, 3, 6 and 10 (`the-demo.qmd:39`, `hedda-screen.svg`).
2. **One "disagrees" line doesn't disagree.** Chapter one's line reads "No printer's manual gave the dash a rule before 1684." That fits with a first rule in 1694, so it doesn't contradict the claim.

Reader B said the second point made them trust the tool's count less. That's damaging in a book whose argument is that an assistant is worth what you can check.

My suggestion:

- Rewrite chapter one's sentence so it actually says 1684.
- Add chapter eight to the screen as a second "agrees" line.
- Change "four places", "four lines" and "the third of the four lines" to five.

The four contradictions at the bottom of the screen stay correct either way. I haven't edited anything; tell me if you want it done.

## Other leads, not acted on

- "I write about software for a living" appears twice, in Index Cards and The Name.
- "in that order" in Em has nothing earlier that sets up an order.
- The "Book: ch. 4" line breaks after "ch." in the source. Rendered it reads normally; only plain-text readers see the break.

## Where things are

- The record is in `provenance/readings/blind-read/`: the README, the frozen prompts, and both readers' reactions and summaries. The raw run records stay outside the book, in Quirework's state directory.
- New config: the persona, the questions, a reader preset, `procedures/isolation.toml` (which refuses a mount path that names the book or the tool), and `provenance/readings` added to the evidence roots.
- `quirework dev check` passes. **Nothing is committed yet.**
- I left `/home/ademar/library/book` (and its manifest beside it) and an early trial packet in `/tmp/sq-probe` in place, because my shell can't delete outside the project. Remove them whenever you like.
- Two Quirework bugs got in the way. The plan compiler would have shown the readers the persona twice, so I set it on each reader in the compiled plan instead; the README records this. The 200-byte minimum is checked against the reader's chat reply rather than the file it wrote, which is what stopped Reader A's closing turn.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the five gates on every commit since a base, in a throwaway worktree.
set -u
base=$1
tree=$(mktemp -d)
git worktree add -q --detach "$tree" HEAD
cd "$tree" || exit 1
for sha in $(git rev-list --reverse "$base"..HEAD); do
  git checkout -q "$sha"
  if quirework spec units --check >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    quirework spec notes --check >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    quirework spec trail --check >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    quirework config check >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    quirework dev check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "pass $(git log -1 --format='%h %s')"
  else
    echo "FAIL $(git log -1 --format='%h %s')"
  fi
done
cd - >/dev/null || exit 1
git worktree remove --force "$tree"

**One thing I got wrong on the way.** I checked the suite by filtering its output for "fail" and "needs", but it reports a broken file as `ABORT`. So most of today's commits first went in with the suite failing, for two reasons:
- an edit of mine merged two marks onto one line in Index Cards' sidecar;
- three paragraphs in `AGENTS.md` and one mark in The Demo's sidecar weren't wrapped to the house width.

Because nothing was pushed, I folded each fix into the commit that caused it and rewrote today's history. Then I checked out each commit in turn and ran the five gates in full, with no filter. All eleven pass.

**The commits:**
1. **Hedda's screen.** Chapter one now says "In 1684 a printer's manual gave the dash its first rule." Chapter eight is on the screen as a second line that agrees. The Demo counts five places and five lines, and the alt text matches. The sidecar used to say "Chapter eight stays off the screen: four places is four places"; it now records your decision instead.
2. **Index Cards.** The script's first complaint, quoted on one line with nothing after it: `ch. 8, line 77: changed. The note says 1684; the sentence says 1694.` Chapter eight's line on Hedda's screen is the same line 77. The spec's escalation section and its trail record this.
3. **The Name.** "I write about software for a living" is gone; that line now reads "I had been meaning to put it under version control for about a month."
4. **The Name, trimmed.** The evening of names keeps the puns line and the colon, and loses the catalog.
5. **Em.** "Then Em read the README: the tool first, the README after, which is the order everyone does it in."
6. **Blind-read setup.** The persona, the questions, the reader preset, and the rule that refuses a mount path naming the book or the tool.
7. **The reading record** in `provenance/readings/blind-read/`: both readers' reactions and summaries, the prompts, and a README covering who read, on what, what it cost, what the receipts proved, and what you decided.
8. **Length.** `AGENTS.md` and the writing procedure now say about seven thousand words. I also removed the "about thirteen hundred words" targets from seven chapter sidecars, because they came from the old figure. Otto's and Full Stop's ceilings stay.

10. **Mounts.** A blind read's copy of the book goes under `~` (`$HOME`, your home). It can't go in `scratchpad/`: the tool refuses any mount inside the project, because a reader with a shell reads its own paths.
11. **The printout's color.** The script's line first printed in the PDF template's default dark teal. I turned code highlighting off in `_quarto.yml`, and it now prints black on gray.
